seoTitle: How to Transfer Shopify Store Ownership
metaDescription: Transfer Shopify store ownership securely by updating the owner's email, assigning a new primary owner, and removing your own access.
intro: Whether you're selling your store, handing it off to a partner, or updating account details, transferring Shopify store ownership needs to be done carefully to avoid losing access mid-process. This guide walks through updating the owner email and making someone else the primary store owner.

steps.heading: Add the new owner as a staff member
steps.body: Invite the person taking over as a staff account on your Shopify store before transferring ownership.

steps.heading: Update the owner's email
steps.body: Go into your account settings to change the store owner's email to the new owner's address.

steps.heading: Assign primary owner status
steps.body: Use Shopify's ownership transfer settings to make the new user the primary owner of the store.

steps.heading: Confirm the transfer
steps.body: Complete any confirmation steps Shopify requires, such as email verification, to finalize the ownership change.

steps.heading: Remove your own access if needed
steps.body: Once the transfer is confirmed and complete, remove your own staff access if you no longer need to be involved with the store.

faq.question: Can I undo a store ownership transfer?
faq.answer: Once ownership is transferred, only the new owner can grant access back to you, so it's important to confirm details before finalizing.

faq.question: Why isn't the ownership transfer showing up in settings?
faq.answer: This can happen if the email change hasn't been confirmed yet or if the new owner hasn't accepted their staff invitation first.

faq.question: Do I need the new owner's permission to transfer ownership?
faq.answer: Yes, the new owner typically needs to accept an invitation and confirm their email before becoming the primary owner.

faq.question: Will billing information transfer automatically?
faq.answer: Billing details are usually tied to the account owner, so the new owner may need to update payment information after the transfer.
